label: OpenRouter
summary: One key, hundreds of models, free and paid side by side.
detail: The easiest place to start. A single key reaches models from every major lab plus a rotating set tagged `:free` that cost nothing at all — enough to use the assistant properly before deciding whether it is worth paying for. Prices are reported per model, so the spend cap works accurately here.
free_tier: Free: a rotating set of models tagged `:free`. One key reaches hundreds of models, free and paid. The easiest place to start.

label: Local model
summary: Free, private, and works with no internet at all.
detail:
Point djmanzo at Ollama or anything else speaking the OpenAI shape on localhost:11434. No key, no account, no cost, and — the part that matters in a booth — no dependency on the venue's wifi. Your track list never leaves the machine.

A small local model handles the DJ vocabulary well, because the task is narrow: turn a sentence into commands from a fixed list. It will not plan a set as well as a frontier model.

label: Anthropic
summary: Strong at instruction-following. Trial credit, then pay as you go.
detail: Good at staying inside a fixed command vocabulary, which is exactly what this application asks of a model. No free tier beyond signup credit, and the model list carries no pricing, so the session cost shows as unknown rather than being guessed at.
free_tier: Trial credit on signup, then pay as you go.

label: OpenAI
summary: Trial credit, then pay as you go.
detail: Works well and is the most widely documented if you want to experiment. Like Anthropic, the model list carries no pricing, so spend is reported as unknown rather than estimated.
free_tier: Trial credit on signup, then pay as you go.

label: Google AI Studio
detail: The most usable free tier of the hosted options, with large context windows. Worth having as a second key even if OpenRouter is the default, so there is somewhere to fall back to when a provider has a bad night.

label: Groq
summary: Free tier, and very fast — which is what voice needs.
detail: Latency is felt directly when you are speaking to something. Groq is the fastest of these by a wide margin, which makes it the right choice once voice control lands. Free tier with rate limits rather than a bill.
free_tier: Free tier, and very fast -- which matters most for voice, where latency is felt directly.
